title.narrative: Safeguarding and strengthening local and national public interest journalism in Mozambique

description.narrative:
This action has been prepared as a response to the current situation in Mozambique, that remains challenging, as the country grapples with increasing poverty rates, recurrent natural disasters, insurgencies in the North and a government increasingly sensitive to criticism. The country¿s freedom of expression is rated ¿Partially Free¿ as journalists who report on corruption or other sensitive issues risk violent attacks. Trust and cooperation between media and government has significantly declined fueling an anti-media sentiment that is reflected in drafted laws further restricting civil society and media. Journalists are facing attacks, including arrests and even abductions. The situation fosters an environment of fear and self-censorship among journalists.

In response to the post electoral crisis IMS requested additional funds to reinforce the component on the safety needs of journalists in Mozambique, after several attacks and threats addressed they faced. The additional funds, IMS will focus on safeguarding staff, journalists and partners, ensuring safety mechanisms, legal aid, first line medical support, Press jackets for ease of identification, first aid kits, equipment replacement in case of loss due to crisis related violent attacks and emergency support to maintain operations, countering disinformation and uphold program continuity.

title.narrative: Country score on the Freedom House Index Freedom of the Press

description.narrative: Freedom of the Press provides analytical reports and numerical scores for 199 countries and territories, continuing a process conducted by Freedom House since 1980. Each country and territory is given a total press freedom score from 0 (best) to 100 (worst) on the basis of 23 methodology questions divided into three subcategories. The total score determines the status designation of Free, Partly Free, or Not Free.

title.narrative: World Press Freedom Index country score according to the Reporters Without Borders (RSF)

description.narrative: The Index is compiled by pooling the responses of experts to a questionnaire devised by the RSF. This qualitative analysis is combined with quantitative data on abuses and acts of violence against journalists during the period evaluated. The criteria evaluated in the questionnaire are pluralism, media independence, media environment and selfcensorship, legislative framework, transparency, and the quality of the infrastructure that supports the production of news and information.Country scores range from 0 to 100 (with 0 being the best possible score and 100 the worst).

comment.narrative: Score 56.13 or better higher
